Checks has no joining edges, as in the capsule study. In the ruined bug cathedral everything moves smoothly, and its glow-bugs fly only while it joins or releases. The bell on a jump ring moves smoothly too, and its bell rings only as the join completes. In couched wire the copper runs smoothly and the needle works tack by tack, while the felt boils on 12 fps steps. In the penannular brooch the silver swings and turns smoothly and only the felt boils. In the swan boat everything moves smoothly: the silver unfurls slowly and the boat dips and rocks under the shell. In ants meet bees the ants walk and the bees fly smoothly, with flickering wings, while the felt boils on 12 fps steps. In the shared quilt, shade the widgets apart and then joined: apart, stone lowers and felt goes under its own quilt; joined, one quilt is unrolled over both. In one line, shade the widgets apart and then joined: apart, Jarvis hangs charms on a brass chain and the felt is pegged out on washing lines; joined, the chain and the cotton are tied into one line. In one hinge, shade the widgets apart and then joined: apart, the stone seat tips up toward you and the elven glass tips back away from you; joined, they tip up together on one rod wound with the silver vine. In bays sewn on, pick Aisle or Nave: each bay is chalked, dropped in, pinned, basted in red, sewn round in cream, has its basting pulled out and its pins taken away, and is then dressed; anything in the way steps aside first and comes back when the bays are unpicked. In storeys, buttoned, pick a size (or press S): Jarvis lays its storeys course by course, smoothly, while GitDiscuss's are dropped on and sewn round on 12 fps steps; each storey brings its own boss and tab, and a joined pair buttons each one across the gap. In wire key, stone lock, turn the key back (drag round it anticlockwise) to draw the bolt, or tap it; the iron knocks at the end of each turn and the wire moves smoothly. In pinned voussoirs, set the Angle row (or drag the wedge up or down, or press ↑ ↓ on it) to open or close the wedge a course at a time, and tap the springer to release; stone and shell both move smoothly. In silvered bone stay, set the Angle row (or drag the stay up or down, or press ↑ ↓ on it): the bone lifts off the moonstone pin while GitDiscuss turns and drops onto the nearest eye when it stops; tap the pin to release. In felt aumbry, press Shade: each display is shoved back into a felt recess, the doors flop shut and the lamp is lit by sewing its flame on. In riveted setting, tap or pull the copper margin round GitDiscuss to pop the rivets; the plate, tabs, rivets and hammer all move smoothly. In one spindle, shade the widgets apart and then joined: apart, Jarvis's leaf is unravelled onto a silver spindle and the felt is frogged onto wooden sticks; joined, the spindle's shaft is pushed through the brooch and GitDiscuss's wool is wound onto it too. In one fan, pick Fanned (or press S) with Checks apart and then docked: apart, felt strips are swept out from behind the cushion on 12 fps steps; docked, the felt fan folds away and the oriel's foot opens smoothly into a stone fan vault. In bead pinion, iron rack, set the Angle row (or drag the rack up or down, or press ↑ ↓ on it): GitDiscuss rolls on the wire beads, a bead in a notch at every 15°, and slides as it tips because it has no fixed pivot; tap the hub to release. In moonstones in keyholes, join, then drag the keyholes up: the tendrils let go first, then GitDiscuss follows your hand up the slots and lets go past halfway (sooner, it drops back on). Everything moves smoothly. In graving dock, tap or pull the slab or the pier to refill the dock and float GitDiscuss off its keel blocks; the stone and the water move smoothly. In blocked on a lancet, pick Lancet or Two lights (or press S): a limewood block rises behind Checks and the steamed felt is drawn up over it in tugs on 12 fps steps, corded, pinned, brushed with shellac, dried and dressed; anything in the way steps aside first. In one weight, set the Angle row apart to fill or vent GitDiscuss's felt balloon, then join: the stone moves smoothly while the felt boils on 12 fps steps; joined, drag the stone weight up or down (or press ↑ ↓ on it) and tap the wheel to release. In bronze first, then ice, tap the seam (or press Enter on it) to thaw the ice and lift the bronze out; the stone, metal and water all move smoothly. In wine-dyed felt, shade the widgets apart and then joined: apart, the stone presses its grapes into a chalice and the felt is ironed; joined, the wine runs along a lead trough into the felt and the iron sets the stain. In pierced lantern, tap or pull the canopy, a rib or the dish to put GitDiscuss's light out and open the lantern; pause either widget while it is held and the thrown pattern burns grey and low. The silver and the light move smoothly. In one field, drag GitDiscuss onto Jarvis for a field of hematite beads, or Jarvis onto GitDiscuss for a field of needles (the Joined button joins onto Jarvis); the other widget's pieces cross the gap and change form in the field, and tapping or pulling the field releases it. Everything there moves smoothly. In one course, shade the widgets apart and then join them: the shell's plates dart smoothly into a course and the felt pieces flop into theirs on 12 fps steps; joined, the two courses slide together until the tab seats in the socket. In hand of justice, pick Galleries (or press S) with the pair apart and then joined: the stone kings rise and the lintel comes down smoothly, the felt folk spring up and the banner unrolls on 12 fps steps; joined, the king on the buttress lowers his rod across the seam and the felt person at the corner takes the stone hand. In moon cradle, tap or pull the crescent or the lacing at either end to unlace GitDiscuss and lift it out; the silver and the silk move smoothly and the felt only boils. In needle-felted crimps, felt pliers squeeze the first roving sleeve and it springs back, so a felting needle stabs every sleeve tight, all on 12 fps steps; pull or tap the crimps and a reverse needle teases them loose. In one frost, shade the widgets apart and then joined: apart, the stone is rained on and dried by a low sun that lights its cut letters, and the leaves frost over; joined, the frost crosses the vine onto the stone, its rain turns to snow and icicles grow. Rain, snow and frost move smoothly. In one ripple, pick Pools (or press S) with the pair apart and then joined: the water's rings run smoothly and pass, while the felt balls are laid ring by ring on 12 fps steps and stay; joined, a last drop falls through the seam and one ring crosses both halves. In jewel case, everything moves on 12 fps steps: the roll unrolls, Jarvis's roving is drawn in and the padding plumps pillow by pillow until it presses GitDiscuss's frame; tap or pull the case (or its button) to undo it. In half a rod each, join, then turn the iron wheel (drag round it), tap it (or press Enter on it) to crank on clockwise to the next 15° mark, or set the Angle row: past a dead centre GitDiscuss swings back, so one turn rocks it down, level, up and back; tap the steel sleeve to release. The iron and the wheel move smoothly and the felt tips over on 12 fps steps. In winged keystone, join, then drag the keystone up out of the cleft (most of the way out, it lets go; short of that it drops back in), or tap it; the stone and the silver move smoothly and the wing spins as it falls. In ruin, cut down, press Shade: the Hollow needle slashes each wall twice where the gothic plan says, the band drops into the fog, the wall is let down and cramped, and a glow-bug lights the joint in the status colour; everything moves smoothly. Felt parts move at 12 frames a second and their fibres shift each frame; stone stays still except in the reliquary bay, where it moves smoothly; in the needle seam the Hollow needle sets a smooth pace and the felt only boils on 12 fps steps; on the iron bracket the stone stays still and the iron moves smoothly; on the tracery the stone stays still and the vine grows smoothly; in the hoop setting the wire moves smoothly; in felt bugs everything is felt, so the pendants and the caterpillar all move at 12 frames a second; in felt caterpillars, tap a shaded caterpillar (or press Enter on its nameplate) to pause or resume its widget; in newel stair, drag the bell up or down the felt stair turret (or press ↑ ↓ on it) to wind GitDiscuss to an angle, and tap the walnut button to release; in felt skep, press Shade: each cord is coiled into a skep and stitched, a bee leaves, and the stitches are snipped so the turns slump flat; displays and dragging stay smooth. Nothing moves at rest.
